## Overview

In pressurized micro-irrigation systems (drip and micro-sprinkler), spatial pressure variation along a lateral pipe directly governs water application uniformity. Because discharge decreases stepwise at each emitter outlet, friction head loss along the lateral is non-linear.

`calc_backstep()` implements the **backstep numerical procedure**: starting from a known boundary pressure head at the distal emitter, it steps upstream segment by segment toward the lateral inlet, computing Darcy-Weisbach friction losses via `hf::calc_head_loss_darcy()`.

```{r load-packages}
library(irritool)
library(ggplot2)
```

---

## 1. Level Lateral Line (`slope = 0`)

Consider a polyethylene drip lateral with internal diameter $D = 0.012\text{ m}$ ($12\text{ mm}$), absolute roughness $\varepsilon = 1.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$, and $50$ emitters spaced at $0.30\text{ m}$ intervals.

Emitter discharge follows $q = k \cdot H^x$ with discharge coefficient $k = 8.84 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}\,\text{mca}^{-x}$ and exponent $x = 0.50$. Assuming a target distal pressure head of $10\text{ mca}$:

```{r flat-lateral}
level_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0,
  emitter_coef = 8.84e-7,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

head(level_profile)
tail(level_profile)
```

Inlet operating pressure head and total lateral inlet flow rate are retrieved from the first row (`emitter == 1`):

```{r inlet-summary}
# Required inlet pressure head (mca)
level_profile$pressure_head[1]

# Total inlet flow rate (m3/s)
level_profile$section_flow[1]
```

---

## 2. Effect of Terrain Slope (`slope`)

The `slope` parameter specifies elevation change per unit length ($\text{m m}^{-1}$):
* **Positive values** (`slope > 0`) represent uphill flow (elevation gain toward the distal end).
* **Negative values** (`slope < 0`) represent downhill flow (elevation drop toward the distal end).

```{r slope-comparison}
uphill_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0.02,
  emitter_coef = 8.84e-7,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

downhill_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = -0.02,
  emitter_coef = 8.84e-7,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

comparison_df <- rbind(
  cbind(level_profile, scenario = "Level (0%)"),
  cbind(uphill_profile, scenario = "Uphill (+2%)"),
  cbind(downhill_profile, scenario = "Downhill (-2%)")
)

ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = emitter, y = pressure_head, color = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Pressure Head Profile Along Lateral Line",
    x = "Emitter Index (1 = Lateral Inlet)",
    y = "Pressure Head (mca)",
    color = "Slope Scenario"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
